correctness.rationale: Zero protection at index i depends only on whether the opposite part has zero, one, or at least two defenders labelled 2; when a unique defender is at matching index i, its paired vertex must be positive. Positive-support totality similarly is automatic when there are ≥2 opposite positives but prohibits a matched isolated unique positive. These conditions are necessary/sufficient, giving seven mutually exclusive contributions: all-ones, one-sided single or multi defender, coincident and distinct single defenders, single+multi defender, and multi+multi. Multiplying allowed one-side polynomials yields the displayed RESULT formula. Independent direct adjacency enumeration of all ternary labelings for n=3,4,5 matches each polynomial coefficient; optimum counts are 31,48,100 respectively. The case proof, not finite checks, covers all n.

value.rationale: Crown graphs are a canonical one-edge-per-vertex perturbation of complete bipartite graphs, introducing precise missing-neighbor effects. A full all-weight enumerator with exact optimum multiplicities is a natural useful graph invariant and goes far beyond a minimum alone; it detects the sharp minimum shift from 4 on K_{n,n} to 6.
